entry_item.definition: [S. mahā-bhūta, "the four great elements"] n. The body conceived as an aggregate of "elements',' organism; matter; element (in nature); constitution; vital principle.

example.definition: To die.

Health, state of health.

Body, organism.

Element .

(fr.S.) T. hbyung ba chen po bzhi; S. catvari maha-bhūtāni. The four 'great' elements which do not derive from anything and are the transcendental bases of certain qualities of earth (sirui), hard; water (usun), flexible; fire (γal), hot; air (salkin) yielding. See next entry.
T. hbyung ba las gyur pa S. bhautika. Originated from the maxabud: material belonging to the sphere of perceptions by the senses.ED 412-3.

example.definition: les éléments extérieurs qui constituent le corps s'étant réunis (causèrent la mort), mais la force intérieure (i.e. l'âme) resta encore. NB. Rentrer dans le pantchatvam i.q. se réunir aux cinq éléments. On suppose que chaque molécule du corps va se réunir à l'élément particulier dont elle est formée
cinq éléments primitifs: la terre, l'atmosphère ou l'air, le feu, l'eau et l'éther. Cf. pantchatva, πεντάϛ, elementorum indicorum, e quibus corpora coalescunt atque in quae dissolvuntur
